area: Grazing rules (grazingStatus, the grazing block of findExceptions, grazingTimeline in app.js)
summary:
The planted case works. On the committed data the dashboard raises exactly one grazing alert, "[serious] Yearlings in Sand Hills | Day 24 of a 21-day plan (3 days over)", and the timeline marks it with "+3d" starting at x=538.2. Both match hand arithmetic (Sep 6 + 21 = Sep 27; Sep 30 is 3 days later). Threshold and plural boundaries, DST and timezone day counting, the two-groups water context, and the hover text also check out. Everything else rests on one assumption: the open stay (blank out_date) is the group's one current location and its pasture_id exactly matches pastures.csv. When that assumption breaks, I reproduced these failures:

(1) HIGH. A mistyped, lower-case or space-padded pasture_id on an open move makes findExceptions throw. The whole dashboard goes blank: 0 tiles, 0 alert rows, no charts, and no error message, so the critical T4 leak and T2 low-tank alerts are hidden.
(2) A bad pasture_id on an old closed move crashes the timeline, and the gain chart, budget chart and rules table never render.
(3) The current stay is chosen by blank out_date, not by as_of. As a result:
  - An out_date after as_of silences a real overrun.
  - Viewing an earlier as_of gives no alerts.
  - A move entered ahead of time silences the Sand Hills alert and puts "Yearlings here now" on the critical Windmill tank alert, though they are not there yet.
  - Following the alert's own advice ("record a new move date") by putting the date in out_date, the only date column, makes the alert disappear.
(4) If a group's old stay is never closed, the dashboard raises a false "15 days over" alert. The chart contradicts it, showing "+3d" twice. A duplicated row doubles the alert.
(5) A group with no open move, no moves, or a blank in_date drops out silently. A blank in_date also blanks the entire timeline (0 of 23 bars drawn).
(6) min_rest_days is never read. The example season itself has two pastures that held two groups at once, and 13 of 15 pasture re-entries short of the pasture's own minimum rest. Two of those are current stays (Cows in South Divide 6 of 60 days; Heifers in Lone Tree 34 of 45). None of this was planted, and the "nothing else" test passes only because no rule looks for it.
(7) The serious action is identical for 1, 30 or 90 days over and names no destination. As of Sep 30 the only rested open pasture is Windmill, whose tank is critically low.

There are also smaller timeline problems: month ticks hard-coded to Jun–Sep 2026, groups missing from groups.csv not drawn, past overstays not marked. Wording issues: "Day 24" counts the arrival day as day 0, a move due on the as-of date reads "Planned move in 0 days", and bad values produce text like "-day plan" or "23.75 days".

All repros are in /home/claude/ranch-ops-dashboard/docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs: 39 cases, 7 controls MATCH, 32 MISMATCH, exit 0, never throws. Without Playwright the browser part is skipped and the rest still runs. That file was already committed as a WIP version in e833ac5. HEAD is e833ac5, which only adds docs/audit files over cfd77e5, so the code reviewed is identical. I rewrote that file and verified every case by running it. It now shows as modified in git status. No other repo file was touched.
trace:
SOURCE ROWS
- moves.csv: group, pasture_id, in_date, out_date. CRLF line endings; parseCSV splits on \r?\n. Dates stay strings and a blank cell becomes "".
- pastures.csv: pasture_id, name, acres, planned_graze_days, min_rest_days. min_rest_days is never read by any code.
- meta.csv: as_of = "2026-09-30T18:00".

CALCULATION: grazingStatus (exceptions.js:54-61)
- Keeps every move with a falsy out_date (exceptions.js:56). That means any number per group; as_of is not considered and in_date is not checked.
- Looks the pasture up by exact string id: byId[m.pasture_id] (:57). A miss leaves p undefined, and p.name throws at :59.
- days = (Date(as_of.slice(0,10)) - Date(in_date)) / 864e5 (:58). For two ISO date-only strings this is a whole number of UTC days. A blank in_date gives NaN; an in_date with a time of day is parsed as local time, giving a fractional count.
- Returns {group, pasture: name, pastureId, inDate, days, planned: planned_graze_days}.

CALCULATION: findExceptions
- whoIsThere(pid) (:99) joins the groups whose open move is in pid. Water alerts use it in their subject: "Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now)".
- Grazing loop (:118-125): over = days - planned.
  - over > 0: serious, subject "<group> in <pasture name>", problem "Day <days> of a <planned>-day plan (<over> day[s] over)", action "Move them, or check the grass and record a new move date".
  - Otherwise, over >= -2 (graceDays): warning, "Planned move in <-over> day[s]", action "Line up the move".
  - NaN fails both tests, so no row.
- Rows are sorted by severity, then area.

DISPLAY: app.js
- findExceptions runs at top level (:222), before anything is drawn, so a throw there leaves the page empty.
- exc feeds the "Needs attention" tile count, the "Grazing (n)" chip and the table row (severity badge | Grazing | subject | problem | action).

DISPLAY: grazingTimeline (app.js:112-147)
- Rows come from groups.csv only (:115).
- The axis runs from the earliest in_date of all moves to the as_of date (:113, :117).
- Month ticks are a fixed list, 2026-06-01..09-01 (:120).
- Each move of a row's group is a bar from in_date to (out_date || as_of). It is green when out_date is blank (:129).
- p = names[pasture_id] has no fallback. p.pasture_id (:140) and p.name (:143) throw for an unknown id.
- current = Object.fromEntries(grazingStatus...) is keyed by group, so the last open move wins (:124). Every green bar of that group takes its over value. If over > 0, a red rect runs from in_date + planned to the as-of line, labelled "+<over>d".
- Hover: "<group> in <name> / <in> to now (<len> days) / Plan: <planned> days".
- Renderers run in sequence (:225): tiles, table, water, grazing, gain, budget, rules. A throw in grazingTimeline stops gain, budget and rules.

COMMITTED DATA WALK
- Yearlings: P3 Sand Hills in 2026-09-06, open, plan 21. Day count = 24, over = 3. Alert: "[serious] Yearlings in Sand Hills | Day 24 of a 21-day plan (3 days over) | Move them, or check the grass and record a new move date". Timeline: red from x = 74 + 118/121*476 = 538.2, label "+3d"; tooltip "Sep 6 to now (24 days) / Plan: 21 days".
- Cows: P7, Sep 12, 18/21, over = -3, no row.
- Heifers: P4, Sep 19, 11/14, over = -3, no row. The Heifers do appear in the T4 water subject.
- Total: 10 alerts, 1 of them grazing.

findings.title: A pasture_id on an open move that is not in pastures.csv blanks the whole dashboard
findings.location: exceptions.js:57-59 (p = byId[m.pasture_id]; p.name); app.js:222 (top-level findExceptions, nothing after it runs)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases G-01, G-02, GB-01). Minimal input: the committed data with the open Yearlings row changed to 'Yearlings,P9,2026-09-06,'. Lower case ('p3') and a trailing space ('P3 ') fail the same way.
findings.expected: findExceptions returns the 9 non-grazing alerts (T2 low, T4 leak, T6 silent, gain, health, budget) plus a data-problem row naming P9. The page shows tiles, the table and the charts.
findings.actual: G-01: "threw TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name') -> findExceptions returns nothing at all"; G-02: "'p3': threw TypeError ...; 'P3 ': threw TypeError ..."; GB-01 in Chromium: "pageErrors=[\"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')\"] asofLine=\"\" tiles=0 alertRows=0 waterCharts=0 grazingChart=false gainChart=false budgetChart=false rulesRows=0". A screenshot shows only static headings: the 'Needs attention' card is empty with no error message.
findings.consequence: One typo in the grazing log, or a pasture renamed in one file and not the other, hides every alert on the ranch. That includes the critical leaking tank (T4) and the critically low tank (T2). The page does not say anything went wrong. An empty 'Needs attention' card reads like an all-clear, so cattle can go without water.
findings.regression_test: Load the committed data. Replace the moves row 'Yearlings,P3,2026-09-06,' with 'Yearlings,P9,2026-09-06,'. Assert that findExceptions does not throw. Assert it returns rows with subjects starting 'Tank T4' (critical) and 'Tank T2' (critical), and at least 9 non-Grazing rows in total: the committed data has 10 alerts, only 1 of them grazing, counted by hand from the test list. Assert exactly one row's problem contains 'P9'. Repeat with 'p3' and 'P3 ' and assert they are either matched to Sand Hills or reported as unknown.
findings.proposed_fix: In grazingStatus, normalise ids with trim() and toUpperCase() when building byId and when looking up. When the pasture is still missing, return {group, pasture: m.pasture_id, pastureId: m.pasture_id, unknown: true} instead of dereferencing undefined. In findExceptions, turn unknown into a serious row such as "Yearlings: pasture P9 isn't in pastures.csv, so the move can't be checked", with the action "Fix the pasture id in moves.csv". In app.js, wrap each renderer and findExceptions in try/catch and print a visible 'could not load X: <message>' line instead of leaving the page blank.

findings.title: A pasture_id not in pastures.csv on any closed move crashes the timeline; the gain chart, budget chart and rules table never render
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases G-C3, GB-02). Input: committed moves plus 'Yearlings,P9,2026-05-01,2026-05-20'.
findings.expected: The exception table (10 rows) still renders, along with the grazing, gain and budget charts and the 12-row rules table. The bad row is drawn with its raw id or flagged.
findings.actual: G-C3 (control): findExceptions is fine, returning the same single Yearlings row. GB-02: "pageErrors=[\"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'pasture_id')\"] ... tiles=5 alertRows=10 waterCharts=8 grazingChart=false gainChart=false budgetChart=false rulesRows=0".
findings.consequence: An old, already-closed log row with a typo (for example from last spring) removes the grazing rotation, the daily-gain chart, the budget chart and table, and the rules table. The alert table still shows. The manager loses the evidence behind the alerts and the thresholds that explain them, and nothing on the page says why.
findings.regression_test: In headless Chromium, load the page with moves.csv plus 'Yearlings,P9,2026-05-01,2026-05-20'. Assert no pageerror. Assert #grazing svg, #gain svg and #budgetChart svg exist. Assert #rules has 12 tr: 11 rules in app.js:204-214 plus a header, counted by hand.
findings.proposed_fix: Use p = names[mv.pasture_id] ?? { pasture_id: mv.pasture_id, name: mv.pasture_id + ' (unknown pasture)', planned_graze_days: '?' }. Wrap each renderer call at app.js:225 in its own try/catch that writes an error note into its card.

findings.title: The current stay is chosen by blank out_date, ignoring as_of: an out_date after as_of, a future move, or an earlier as_of hides or misplaces alerts
findings.repro:
node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases G-05, G-06, G-07, GB-04, GB-05).
- G-05: committed data with the Sand Hills row given out_date 2026-10-03.
- G-06: committed data with as_of 2026-08-20T18:00.
- G-07: Sand Hills closed 2026-10-02 plus an open 'Yearlings,P2,2026-10-02,'.
findings.expected:
- G-05: Sep 6 + 21 = Sep 27, so as of Sep 30 the alert is '[serious] Yearlings in Sand Hills ... (3 days over)'.
- G-06: Cows were in Cedar Draw from Jul 31 on an 18-day plan, due Aug 18, so on Aug 20 there should be one row '[serious] Cows in Cedar Draw ... (2 days over)'.
- G-07: the same Sand Hills alert, and T2's subject is 'Tank T2 (Windmill)': nobody has been in Windmill since Aug 11.
- GB-04/05: the Sand Hills bar stays green, ends at the as-of line (x <= 550) and carries '+3d'.
findings.actual:
- G-05: "(no rows)  ## grazingStatus places the Yearlings in: (nowhere)".
- G-06: "(no rows)  ## grazingStatus: Cows@P7 days=-23, Heifers@P4 days=-30, Yearlings@P3 days=-17".
- G-07: "grazing: (no rows)  ## T2: [critical] Tank T2 (Windmill, Yearlings here now)".
- GB-04: "last Yearlings bar x=456.6 right end=560.8 current=false; overrun labels=[]", i.e. drawn grey and past the as-of line (x(Oct 3) = 74 + 124/121*476 = 561.8).
- GB-05: "current bars on the Yearlings row: [{x:558.9,w:1,...cur:true}]; overrun labels=[]".
findings.consequence: The alert's own advice is to 'record a new move date'. The only date column is out_date. A manager who writes the planned move date there closes the stay, and the 3-days-over alert disappears even though the cattle have not moved: a misleading all-clear. A move entered a day ahead silences the real overrun too. It also tells the crew the yearlings are drinking at Windmill, the critically low tank, when they are not there yet. That sends someone to the wrong place, or makes a dry tank look like an emergency for cattle that aren't on it. Setting as_of back to review an earlier date shows no grazing problems at all.
findings.regression_test:
Hand-computed:
(a) Moves = committed, with the Yearlings Sand Hills row given out_date 2026-10-03, as_of 2026-09-30T18:00. Expect exactly one grazing row: severity serious, subject 'Yearlings in Sand Hills', problem containing '(3 days over)'.
(b) Committed moves, as_of 2026-08-20T18:00. Expect exactly one grazing row: 'Cows in Cedar Draw', '(2 days over)'. Heifers are due Aug 26 and Yearlings Aug 25, both outside the 2-day grace.
(c) Sand Hills closed 2026-10-02 plus open 'Yearlings,P2,2026-10-02'. Expect the 'Yearlings in Sand Hills' serious row, and the T2 subject exactly 'Tank T2 (Windmill)'.
findings.proposed_fix: Define current relative to as_of. Let asOfDate = as_of.slice(0,10). A move is current when in_date <= asOfDate and (out_date is blank or out_date > asOfDate). Pick at most one per group: the latest in_date. Use the same predicate in app.js for cur, and clip bar ends to asOfDate. Add an optional planned_move_date column to moves.csv for 'record a new move date'. Change the action text to name it, so following the advice does not close the stay.

findings.title: A group with two open moves gets a false '15 days over' alert, and the timeline contradicts it; a duplicated row doubles the alert
findings.location: exceptions.js:56 (no one-current-stay-per-group rule); exceptions.js:118-125; app.js:124 (current keyed by group, last wins), :129-138
findings.repro:
node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases G-03, G-04, GB-03).
- G-03/GB-03: committed moves with 'Yearlings,P7,2026-08-25,2026-09-06' changed to 'Yearlings,P7,2026-08-25,'.
- G-04: the committed moves plus a second copy of 'Yearlings,P3,2026-09-06,'.
findings.expected:
- G-03: one Yearlings row (Sand Hills, 3 days over) and ideally a data warning about the stale open row. No 'South Divide' row.
- G-04: one grazing row, 10 alerts in total.
- GB-03: the chart agrees with the table.
findings.actual:
- G-03: "[serious] Yearlings in South Divide | Day 36 of a 21-day plan (15 days over) | ...  ||  [serious] Yearlings in Sand Hills | Day 24 of a 21-day plan (3 days over) | ...".
- G-04: "11 alerts in total; grazing: [serious] Yearlings in Sand Hills ... || [serious] Yearlings in Sand Hills ...".
- GB-03: "overrun labels: [{\"s\":\"+3d\",\"x\":549},{\"s\":\"+3d\",\"x\":549}] ## red: [{x:491,w:58},{x:538.2,w:10.8}] ## current bars: [{x:409.4,w:139.6,cur:true},{x:456.6,w:92.4,cur:true}]". A screenshot shows one long green P7+P3 bar labelled '+3d'. The 15-day red segment is painted underneath the Sand Hills bar.
findings.consequence: Forgetting to close the previous move, the most common grazing-log slip, produces a false serious alarm. It says 150 yearlings are 15 days over in a pasture they left on Sep 6. The chart beside it says +3d, so the manager cannot tell which to believe. The group is also listed as 'here now' on any water alert in the old pasture. A duplicated export row inflates the 'Needs attention' count.
findings.regression_test: For G-03 moves: assert the grazing rows whose subject starts with 'Yearlings' are exactly one serious 'Yearlings in Sand Hills' containing '(3 days over)', plus at most one data warning naming both 'South Divide' and 'Sand Hills'. Assert no row contains '15 days over'. Hand: Aug 25 + 21 = Sep 15, which is 15 days before Sep 30, the value that must not appear. For G-04: assert findExceptions(...).length === 10 and one grazing row.
findings.proposed_fix: Per group, keep only the latest current stay (see the as_of finding). If a group has more than one open row, emit a warning such as "Yearlings have 2 open moves (South Divide since Aug 25, Sand Hills since Sep 6): close the older one". Drop exact duplicate rows before judging. In app.js, set cur = (mv === currentMove[g]) instead of !mv.out_date, so only one bar is green and the overrun mark uses that bar's own plan.

findings.title: Groups with no usable current stay drop out silently; a blank in_date also blanks the whole timeline
findings.location: exceptions.js:56-60 (only open moves considered; NaN days fail both comparisons at :120 and :123); app.js:113 (start = sorted in_dates [0] = '' when one is blank), :117-118
findings.repro:
node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases G-08, G-09, GB-07, GB-08).
- G-08: the Sand Hills row closed 2026-09-28 with no next move.
- G-09/GB-08: the open row's in_date blanked ('Yearlings,P3,,').
- GB-07: 'Bulls,herd bulls,6,0.0' added to groups.csv.
findings.expected: A row saying the Yearlings (150 head) have no current pasture on record, or a data-problem row for the blank in_date. The other 22 timeline bars still drawn. The Bulls row labelled 'no pasture on record'.
findings.actual:
- G-08: "grazing rows naming Yearlings: (no rows)  ## groups with a current pasture: Cows, Heifers  ## total alerts 9".
- G-09: "(no rows)  ## grazingStatus days=NaN -> over=NaN; (NaN > 0) and (NaN >= -2) are both false".
- GB-08: "bars with a numeric x: 0 of 23; months=Jun@x=NaN Jul@x=NaN Aug@x=NaN Sep@x=NaN; ... alert rows total: 9". The console shows 'Error: <line> attribute x1: Expected length, "NaN"'.
- GB-07: "timeline rows=[Cows,Heifers,Yearlings,Bulls]; bars on the Bulls row=0; alert rows naming Bulls=0".
findings.consequence: 150 head can vanish from the grazing report because the next move wasn't keyed in, or the date cell was left blank. The report then shows fewer problems, not more. A single blank date also wipes the entire rotation chart for all groups, again with no message on the page.
findings.regression_test:
- G-08 moves: assert some row has area 'Grazing', a subject or problem containing 'Yearlings', and text matching /no current pasture|location/i.
- Blank in_date: assert a row whose problem mentions the missing date for Yearlings.
- In the browser, with the blank in_date, assert 22 bars have finite x: 23 bars in the committed data (6 + 10 + 7 rows, counted from moves.csv) minus the bad one.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate each move: in_date must parse, and out_date, when present, must be >= in_date. Report invalid rows as data-problem rows instead of computing NaN. For every group in groups.csv with no current stay as of as_of, push a warning: '<group> (<head> head): no current pasture recorded'. In the timeline, compute start only from valid in_dates and skip invalid rows with a visible note.

findings.title: min_rest_days is never read: current stays started inside the pasture's own minimum rest go unflagged
findings.location: exceptions.js:54-61 and :118-125 (no rest logic); data/pastures.csv column min_rest_days; README.md 'pastures.csv ... minimum rest days'
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases G-14, G-15). Committed data, unchanged.
findings.expected: The rest is computed by hand as in_date minus the last out_date in that pasture by any group. Two rows: Cows in South Divide, where the Yearlings left Sep 6 and the Cows entered Sep 12, giving 6 days of a 60-day minimum. Heifers in Lone Tree, left Aug 16 and re-entered Sep 19, giving 15 + 19 = 34 of 45. (Yearlings in Sand Hills: 76 of 60, fine.)
findings.actual: G-14: "exceptions.js: 0 references, app.js: 0 references". G-15: "rows mentioning rest: 0  ## occupancy calendar says: Cows@P7 rest 6/60, Heifers@P4 rest 34/45, Yearlings@P3 rest 76/60".
findings.consequence: Rest is the other half of a rotation. The column is in the data model and the README, so a reader assumes it is enforced. As it stands, the dashboard says nothing while 180 pairs graze a pasture 54 days short of its rest. Re-grazing too early is how a rotation damages the range. A grazing-literate reviewer will spot this.
findings.regression_test: On the committed data, assert two rows whose problem matches /rest/i: one with subject 'Cows in South Divide' containing '6' and '60', one with 'Heifers in Lone Tree' containing '34' and '45'. The numbers are hand-computed above. Note that the existing 'nothing else' test (length 10) must then become 12, or the data must change (see the data finding).
findings.proposed_fix: In grazingStatus, compute restBefore = in_date minus the latest out_date in the same pasture before this in_date, across all groups. In findExceptions, add a warning when restBefore < min_rest_days, e.g. 'Went in after 6 of 60 rest days'. Add the rule to RULES, the rules table and the README.

findings.title: The example season is not credible as a rotation: two pastures held two groups at once, and 13 of 15 re-entries are short of min rest, none planted or reported
findings.location: scripts/generate_data.py:51-66 (moves(): each group's plan built independently, with no shared pasture calendar); tests/exceptions.test.mjs:26-28 ('nothing else' asserts 10)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (case G-16), which uses a day-by-day occupancy calendar. A separate Python gap computation over data/moves.csv gave the same counts: 15 re-entries, 13 SHORT, overlaps on P2 and P4.
findings.expected: For an example presented as a realistic season: no unplanned pasture sharing and re-entries respecting min_rest_days. Otherwise the dashboard reports them. Hand-checked overlaps: Windmill Jul 24-30 (Cows Jul 13-31 with Yearlings Jul 24-Aug 11); Lone Tree Jun 25-Jul 5 (Yearlings Jun 22-Jul 6 with Heifers Jun 25-Jul 9).
findings.actual: "pastures with two groups at once: P2 2026-07-24..2026-07-30 (7 days, Cows+Yearlings); P4 2026-06-25..2026-07-05 (11 days, Heifers+Yearlings)  ## stays re-entering a grazed pasture: 15, of them short of min rest: 13  ## dashboard rows about any of this: 0". Examples from the Python check: 'P5 Creek Bottom Heifers in 2026-08-26 prev out 2026-08-25 rest 1 min 45 SHORT'; 'P6 Cedar Draw Cows in 2026-07-31 prev out 2026-07-24 rest 7 min 45 SHORT'.
findings.consequence: The portfolio claims the report 'finds exactly the 10 problems that were planted and nothing else'. That holds only because no rule looks at rest or sharing. A ranch-manager reviewer reading moves.csv or the rotation chart will see cattle sent back into pastures 1-7 days after the last group left, against the file's own 45-60 day minimums. That reads as not knowing how a rotation works, which undercuts the operational credibility the piece is meant to show.
findings.regression_test: A data test over data/moves.csv and data/pastures.csv, using an independent day-by-day occupancy calendar. Assert no date on which a pasture holds two groups, unless that pasture and date are listed in PLANTED. For every stay that re-enters a pasture, assert (in_date - previous out_date) >= min_rest_days, unless it is listed in PLANTED. Today the expected counts are 0 overlaps and 0 short rests; the current data gives 2 and 13.
findings.proposed_fix: Rebuild moves() in generate_data.py with one shared pasture calendar. Assign each group the next unoccupied pasture whose rest >= min_rest_days, and adjust the planned days or pasture count so a 3-group, 8-pasture rotation is feasible. Then plant one or two rest or sharing problems deliberately, list them in PLANTED and the README, add the rest rule, and update the 'nothing else' count.

findings.title: The serious grazing action is a blanket line based only on elapsed days: no escalation, no destination, and 'record a new move date' has nowhere to go
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases G-18, G-19). G-18: one open Sand Hills move with in_date 2026-09-08, 2026-08-10 or 2026-06-11. G-19: committed data.
findings.expected: Advice or severity that scales with the overrun (1 vs 30 vs 90 days). A first step that names where the group can go: an unoccupied pasture past its min rest with working water. A 'new move date' that can be recorded without closing the stay.
findings.actual: G-18: "[serious] Day 22 of a 21-day plan (1 day over) -> Move them, or check the grass and record a new move date  ##  [serious] Day 51 ... (30 days over) -> (same)  ##  [serious] Day 111 ... (90 days over) -> (same)". G-19: "free pastures (rest/min): P1 North Flat 18/45, P2 Windmill 50/45 READY, P5 Creek Bottom 21/45, P6 Cedar Draw 39/45, P8 Home Trap 11/30  ## grazing: Move them, or check the grass and record a new move date  ## T2: [critical] Tank T2 (Windmill) | Down to 11.8% full".
findings.consequence: A crew lead gets 'Move them' with no destination. On this data the only pasture that is open and rested is Windmill, and its tank is critically low. Moving the yearlings there as advised puts 150 head on a nearly dry tank. Re-grazing a rested pasture instead breaks min rest. The dashboard holds all three facts but never connects them. A 90-day overrun is ranked the same as a 1-day one. 'Record a new move date' can only be done by writing out_date, which silences the alert (see the as_of finding).
findings.regression_test: On committed data, assert the Yearlings grazing action mentions 'Windmill' and its tank problem, or says no rested pasture has water. Hand: Windmill rest Sep 30 - Aug 11 = 50 >= 45, and T2 is 11.8% < 25. Assert the severity for in_date 2026-06-11 (90 over, by hand: due Jul 2, then 29 + 31 + 30 = 90) differs from the severity for 2026-09-08 (1 over), if escalation is adopted.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a planned_move_date (extension) column to moves.csv and judge against it when present. Escalate to critical past a threshold, e.g. over > max(7, planned*0.25). Build the action from the data: list unoccupied pastures past min rest, and drop or annotate any whose tank has an open water alert. For example: 'Move them: Windmill is the only rested pasture, but its tank is at 11.8%, so fix the float first or haul water'.

findings.title: Two groups in one pasture are each judged alone against a single per-pasture plan
findings.location: exceptions.js:54-61, :118-125 (planned_graze_days per pasture, no head or stocking term)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (case G-17). Heifers leave Lone Tree 2026-09-25 and enter South Divide (P7), joining the Cows.
findings.expected: At least a note that South Divide carries Cows (180 pairs) and Heifers (45) together, with the plan shortened or flagged.
findings.actual: "rows naming South Divide: (no rows)  ## grazingStatus in P7: Cows day 18 of 21, Heifers day 5 of 21". (Control G-C5 shows the water context names both groups correctly: 'Tank T4 (South Divide, Cows and Heifers here now)'.)
findings.consequence: When groups are combined, the grass goes faster than the one-group plan assumes. The dashboard keeps showing both groups as inside plan until the pasture is overgrazed.
findings.regression_test: With the G-17 moves, assert a Grazing row whose subject includes 'South Divide' and whose text names both 'Cows' and 'Heifers'.
findings.proposed_fix: At minimum, emit an informational warning when two or more groups are current in one pasture. Better: store pasture capacity as animal-unit-days, and track consumption as the sum over groups of head x AU factor x days.

findings.title: Timeline month ticks are hard-coded to Jun-Sep 2026
findings.repro:
node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases GB-09..GB-12):
- GB-09: adds 'Cows,P8,2026-04-15,2026-06-01'.
- GB-10: a season starting Jun 15.
- GB-11: every '2026-' replaced by '2025-'.
- GB-12: every date in every CSV shifted +20 days, as_of Oct 20.
findings.expected:
Labels on the first of each month inside the axis:
- GB-09: May,Jun,Jul,Aug,Sep.
- GB-10: Jul,Aug,Sep, all x >= 74.
- GB-11: Jun..Sep inside x 74..560.
- GB-12: Jul,Aug,Sep,Oct.
findings.actual:
- GB-09: "months=Jun@x=210.2 Jul@x=295.2 Aug@x=383 Sep@x=470.8" (no May).
- GB-10: "months=Jun@x=14.7 ...": the Jun gridline and label are drawn in the group-name column. Hand: 74 - 14/107*476 = 11.7, +3.
- GB-11: "months=Jun@x=1512.9 Jul@x=1630.9 Aug@x=1752.8 Sep@x=1874.8 (viewBox width 560)": no month labels visible (screenshot confirmed).
- GB-12: "months=Jun@x=-1.7 Jul@x=116.3 Aug@x=238.3 Sep@x=360.2" (no Oct).
findings.consequence: With real data from any other season, the rotation chart has no month labels, or labels in the wrong place, so a manager cannot read dates off it. Today is mid-October 2026, so even this ranch's own next export (as_of in October) would get no October tick.
findings.regression_test: In headless Chromium, read the month-label text and x positions for each input above. Expected label sets were worked by hand from the calendar: GB-09 May,Jun,Jul,Aug,Sep; GB-10 Jul,Aug,Sep; GB-11 Jun,Jul,Aug,Sep; GB-12 Jul,Aug,Sep,Oct. Assert every x lies within 74..550.
findings.proposed_fix: Generate ticks from the data: start at the first day of the month after start (or start itself if it falls on the 1st), step one month until asOf, and label each with toLocaleDateString(month:'short'). Add the year when the span crosses a year boundary.

findings.title: A group in moves.csv but not in groups.csv is alerted but never drawn on the timeline
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases G-C4, GB-06). Committed moves plus 'Bulls,P8,2026-09-01,'.
findings.expected: The table alert 'Bulls in Home Trap ... (19 days over)' (Sep 1 + 10 = Sep 11, 19 days before Sep 30), and a Bulls row on the timeline. Or the unknown group flagged as a data problem.
findings.actual: G-C4: "[serious] Bulls in Home Trap | Day 29 of a 10-day plan (19 days over)". GB-06: "alert rows naming Bulls=1; timeline rows=[\"Cows\",\"Heifers\",\"Yearlings\"]".
findings.consequence: The alert points to the chart for context, but the chart has no row for that group. The 'Head on grass' tile also leaves those animals out. The same happens on a name mismatch such as 'yearlings' vs 'Yearlings'.
findings.regression_test: In the browser with the Bulls move, assert the timeline's text.lbl includes 'Bulls', or that a Grazing data row says 'Bulls is not in groups.csv'.
findings.proposed_fix: Build the row list as groups.csv order plus any extra groups found in moves, and flag the extras as data problems. Optionally normalise group names with trim and case-folding.

findings.title: Wording: 'Day N' counts the arrival day as day 0, and a move due today reads 'Planned move in 0 days'
findings.location: exceptions.js:121 (`Day ${g.days} of a ${g.planned}-day plan`), :124 (`Planned move in ${-over} day...`)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases G-12, G-13). G-12: committed data. G-13: one open Sand Hills move with in_date 2026-09-09.
findings.expected:
- G-12: arrival Sep 6, as-of Sep 30. Counting the arrival day as Day 1 (Sep 6 = 1, Sep 7 = 2, ...), Sep 30 is Day 25. Elapsed is 24 days. So either 'Day 25 of a 21-day plan' or '24 days in'. '(3 days over)' is right: the planned move was Sep 27.
- G-13: Sep 9 + 21 = Sep 30 = as-of, so the text should say 'today'.
findings.actual: G-12: "Day 24 of a 21-day plan (3 days over)". G-13: "[warning] Yearlings in Sand Hills | Planned move in 0 days | Line up the move".
findings.consequence: Small, but this is a credibility piece. Most ranch records count the day they went in as day 1, so 'Day 24' reads one day short. 'Day 25 ... (3 days over)' would look inconsistent too, so wording by elapsed days is cleaner. 'In 0 days' reads like a bug.
findings.regression_test: Committed data: assert the problem equals '24 days in, 3 days past the planned move (Sep 27)' or matches /Day 25 |24 days in/. in_date 2026-09-09: assert the warning problem matches /today/i.
findings.proposed_fix: Word the serious alert by elapsed days and the due date: `${days} days in; move was due ${fmt(in+planned)} (${over} day(s) ago)`. Use 'Planned move is today' when over === 0.

findings.title: Bad values produce garbled or fractional alert text (blank planned_graze_days, an in_date with a time)
findings.location: exceptions.js:58 (days uses as_of date-only vs a raw in_date), :119-121 (no check that planned is a number)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (cases G-10, G-11). G-10: one open move with in_date '2026-09-06T06:00' (TZ=UTC). G-11: P3's planned_graze_days blanked.
findings.expected:
- G-10: whole days, 'Day 24 of a 21-day plan (3 days over)'.
- G-11: a 'no plan recorded for Sand Hills' row; never 'a -day plan'.
findings.actual: G-10: "[serious] Yearlings in Sand Hills | Day 23.75 of a 21-day plan (2.75 days over) | ...". G-11: "[serious] Yearlings in Sand Hills | Day 24 of a -day plan (24 days over) | ...".
findings.consequence: Exports from real grazing apps often carry times or leave a new pasture's plan blank. The result is a serious alert with nonsense numbers ('-day plan', '2.75 days'), which undermines trust in the whole report. The value of G-10 also depends on the viewer's timezone, because the in_date is parsed as local time.
findings.regression_test: in_date '2026-09-06T06:00' with as_of 2026-09-30T18:00: assert the problem contains 'Day 24' or '24 days' and '(3 days over)', not a decimal. Hand: whole calendar days Sep 6 to Sep 30 = 24; due Sep 27, so 3 over. Blank plan: assert no row text matches / -day plan/, and a row mentions 'no plan'.
findings.proposed_fix: Take in_date.slice(0,10) before computing days. When planned_graze_days is not a positive number, emit a data-problem row ('No planned graze days for Sand Hills') instead of judging against 0.

findings.title: Past overstays are never marked on the timeline (Cows: 22 days on an 18-day plan in Cedar Draw)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/grazing.repro.mjs (case GB-13). Committed data. The hover tooltip reads 'Cows in Cedar Draw / Jul 31 to Aug 22 (22 days) / Plan: 18 days'.
findings.expected: The card note says 'days past the planned move are marked', so a '+4d' mark should appear on the Cows' Cedar Draw bar (22 - 18 = 4), alongside the Yearlings' '+3d'.
findings.consequence: A season review cannot see which past moves ran long. The Cows' 4-day overstay, which is in the example data but not planted, is visible only by hovering.
findings.regression_test: On committed data, assert an overrun label '+4d' on the Cows row, from hand arithmetic: Jul 31 + 18 = Aug 18 and out Aug 22. Also assert the existing '+3d' on the Yearlings row.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute over for every stay as (out_date || asOf) - in_date - planned. Draw the red segment and label for closed stays too, in a muted tone, or reword the card note to 'the current stay's days past plan are marked'.

checked_ok: The committed data gives exactly the planted grazing alert. G-C1 actual: "[serious] Yearlings in Sand Hills | Day 24 of a 21-day plan (3 days over) | Move them, or check the grass and record a new move date". Hand check: Sep 6 + 21 = Sep 27, and Sep 30 is 3 days later. Cows (due Oct 3) and Heifers (due Oct 3) are correctly outside the 2-day grace.

Thresholds and plurals are right at the boundaries. G-C2 actual: "s8: ... (1 day over) ## s10: [warning] ... Planned move in 1 day ## s11: [warning] ... Planned move in 2 days ## s12: (no rows)". This matches the rules-table text 'A planned move is 2 days away or less' (app.js:208).

The 'days over' count is consistent with the move date (in_date + planned_graze_days). The hover tooltip agrees with the alert: "Yearlings in Sand Hills / Sep 6 to now (24 days) / Plan: 21 days" (Chromium hover).

Day counts are whole and timezone-independent for ISO date-only inputs, including across DST changes. With TZ=UTC, America/Denver, Pacific/Auckland and Asia/Kolkata, Oct 20 -> Nov 10 gave 21 and Mar 1 -> Mar 22 gave 21 in every zone.
An unknown pasture_id on a closed move does not affect findExceptions (G-C3 MATCH). Only open moves are judged.
A group missing from groups.csv still gets its grazing alert (G-C4 actual: "[serious] Bulls in Home Trap | Day 29 of a 10-day plan (19 days over)").
Two groups in one pasture are both named in the water context (G-C5 actual: "Tank T4 (South Divide, Cows and Heifers here now)").
An overlapping closed stay does not change the alerts (G-C6 MATCH).

Timeline geometry on the committed data matches hand arithmetic (GB-C0): red segment at x=538.2 (74 + 118/121*476), one '+3d' label, month labels Jun@77 Jul@195 Aug@317 Sep@438.9 inside the plot, no page errors, 10 alert rows, 5 tiles, 12 rules rows.
The existing unit tests pass on the reviewed code: node --test tests/exceptions.test.mjs gives '# tests 8 # pass 8 # fail 0'.

The code under review is identical to cfd77e5: git diff cfd77e5 HEAD --stat over app.js, exceptions.js, index.html, data, scripts, tests, README.md and .github printed nothing. HEAD e833ac5 only adds docs/audit files.
parseCSV handles the CRLF line endings the Python generator writes (od -c shows \r\n; the 23 moves parse, and grazingStatus returns the 3 expected open stays).
